title: Simulating Foraging Decisions
beats: Meet the blob; goal is first step toward a simulated economy; sponsor mention.
Each tree gives one mango a day; trees regrow.
Decision has two inputs: what is possible, what makes it happiest.
Blob collects only mangoes (17) then only wood (14, slower to chop).
Graph of mangoes vs wood; plot extremes, then one mango then wood, then two, three, four mangoes.
Name arrives after the points: production possibilities frontier/curve; curve needs big numbers.
Now what does the blob want? Not full human experience, just choose between two options.
Give every mango/wood combination a happiness score; first mango = 100 (made up), second 60.
Diminishing returns, also marginal utility; logarithm used, explained as inverse of exponential with a 'don't worry' reassurance.
Utility function is an assumption; counter cases (palate, overeating); behavioural economics.
Add wood: two inputs one output becomes a 3D surface; pause and rewind invitation.
Blob tries different mango counts each day to find the maximum, learning like real life.
Equal values: 10 mangoes 9 wood or 9 and 10.
Baby blob doubles mango value; predict; 13 mangoes 6 wood, not twice as many.
Trees give two mangoes: predict; 12 and 10, only a few more mangoes.
Cheaper gordita: eat more but also buy a bigger drink; hard to predict balance.
Next: blob meets neighbour and trades.

metrics.examples: 3 test scenarios, growing in surprise: equal values, baby doubles mango value, trees double production
metrics.ending: Analogy to explain why, then teaser for trade

new_moves.name: pause-and-rewind-permission
new_moves.what: After a dense stretch explicitly tell the learner it is a lot and invite re-listening

new_moves.name: made-up-number-disclosure
new_moves.what: Say the numbers are invented so the learner knows they are scaffolding not facts

new_moves.name: counterintuitive-run
new_moves.what: Choose test cases where the intuitive answer (double) is wrong

theory: The video builds two independent pieces (what is possible, what is wanted) from literal acting-out, then combines them and lets learner predict. Its strongest trick is picking test cases where the obvious guess is wrong, so the learner experiences why optimisation interacts. Notation and names come only after points have been plotted.
velocity: Scene builder: plot points live as the blob acts them out, name the curve only after the points exist.
Orchestrator: after dense stretch, emit a pause/rewind permission beat and insert an explicit recap.
Evals: choose predict-prompt cases where the intuitive guess is wrong.
Voice: say when a number or function is an assumption.
quote: we're going to try to give a happiness score to every possible combination
